architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept acrylic-only strong drift suppression if the repeat-mean SI_15_60 is below 3.80%. This is below one-half of the preregistered 7.61% linear-dilution comparator for reactive mass fraction 0.8000 and favors H-RESIN over H-CORE and H-DUAL, subject to the missing E2-core baseline limitation.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: S1C49 is an AC1920-modified chemistry outside the family supporting the shared 80-130 C thermal-response shape. However, the selected observable is measured directly at 120 C and does not depend on that rheological regularity, so M-HOLD-120 is admissible under the advisory audit. The result supports only a formulation-level drift comparison; it cannot establish a molecular mechanism or validate shared-shape transfer.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If repeat-mean SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, falsify H-RESIN for this acrylic-only composition; H-CORE and H-DUAL remain entangled. If repeat-mean SI_15_60 is below 3.80%, falsify H-CORE and H-DUAL because acrylic alone has reached the registered low-drift regime. A result from 3.80% through 7.60% falsifies none of the three hypotheses at the registered strong-suppression thresholds.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, run a matched-reactive-fraction dual-axis 120 C hold with 15 wt% AC1920 and 5 wt% TK100, together with a contemporaneous unmodified-E2 hold baseline. Randomize preparation order, use independent preparations, and calculate the dilution comparator from the measured E2 drift rather than E1.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Arithmetic mean across at least two independent preparations of SI_15_60 = 100 × (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, measured during the 120 C hold.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C49::M-HOLD-120 directly measures the declared failure mode while testing whether acrylic modification alone can enter the low-drift regime. It sacrifices some ranked mitigation value to resolve the central modifier-axis question, avoids unsupported thermal-shape transfer, and confines any conclusion to formulation-level rheological suppression.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Robustness Adjudicator's S1C49 choice and the Skeptic's hypothesis-coverage argument rather than the Proposer's tied-top S1C41 choice. S1C41 has higher deterministic VOI and mitigation value but leaves H-RESIN versus H-DUAL inseparable because both modifier axes are active. S1C49 is the acrylic-only condition at the same 0.8000 reactive fraction and therefore supplies the more informative one-card probe. I retain the Skeptic's warning that the absent E2 hold baseline prevents unique attribution against H-CORE.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: Only E1 and E5 have original hold trajectories, each from one run. No unmodified-E2 hold baseline exists, and AC1920 functionality is unverified; consequently the E1-derived 7.61% comparator gives conditional rather than unique attribution.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: The drift endpoint itself requires no temperature extrapolation or shared-shape transfer. The principal extrapolation is using E1 drift to predict dilution behavior for an E2-based, AC1920-modified candidate.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The declared discrimination limit is 2.00 percentage points. At least two independent preparations are required, and threshold adjudication is preregistered on their arithmetic mean; individual repeat values must also be reported to expose discordance.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: E2 showed 2.80-3.57× between-preparation viscosity-scale spread. M-HOLD-120 does not itself control that state variation, so preparation history must be recorded and independent preparations used.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local temperature-response regularity was measured in the original E1-E3 reactive PUR chemistry family over 80-130 C, with E1 +P retained only as a separate verified phosphoric-acid perturbation check. The intended mechanistic experiment would retain the E2 reactive-core anchor but introduce acrylic-like and potentially minor tackifier-like modifiers, so it is not yet demonstrated to remain inside the chemistry support of the shared thermal-response regularity. That regularity must not be transferred until chemistry applicability is audited; otherwise a direct temperature sweep is required.
planner.failure_mode: Excessive viscosity growth during prolonged isothermal melt residence at 120 C.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal hold showed a measured 15-to-60 min relative viscosity increase of 51.54% at 120 C, compared with 9.51% for the least-drifting original reference E1.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have local 120 C hold trajectories, each represented by one four-point run over 15-90 min. Their 15-to-60 min changes differ strongly, at 9.51% and 51.54%, but there are no independent hold repeats or systematic acrylic-only versus dual-axis comparisons. In contrast, temperature response is covered by multiple six-point 80-130 C sweeps, and realized viscosity-level variability is at least directly quantified for E2 across three runs.
measurement_requirements: Use a matched-window 120 C hold and record viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min, with at least two independent preparations per composition.
Report the direct SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 observable in percent without extrapolation or imputation.
Include an acrylic-only condition and a condition with a non-zero minor tackifier-like fraction, designed so reactive mass fraction is matched or explicitly accounted for.

Precompute the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction from the measured E1 15-to-60 min drift and each composition's reactive mass fraction; compare measured drift against both that prediction and the registered H-RESIN one-half threshold using the 2 percentage-point measurement discrimination limit.
Record preparation and process history and use independent repeats so realization-state variation is not mistaken for a modifier effect.

Measure the realized viscosity level at a common temperature within the established support, because the acrylic-like axis may primarily relocate viscosity level even if it does not suppress hold drift.
If chemistry-shape applicability is not established for either modified composition, perform a direct 80-130 C sweep rather than relying on one-point shared-shape calibration.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and matched 120 C residence window, does modifier addition leave viscosity drift consistent with linear dilution of the reactive core, suppress drift substantially below one-half of that prediction with the acrylic-like axis alone, or require a non-zero minor tackifier-like axis to reach the low-drift regime? These outcomes distinguish H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: S1C41 is outside the chemistry family in which the shared temperature-response shape was measured, but M-HOLD-120 does not transfer or fit that regularity. It directly observes thermal-hold drift and is therefore chemistry-applicable despite the unvalidated resin-modified thermal shape. Its 15 wt% acrylic-like and 5 wt% minor-tackifier-like levels are both inside externally supported intervention regions.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is below 3.80% across at least two repeats, drift is below half the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction for reactive mass fraction 0.8000. This supports H-RESIN and falsifies H-CORE at the registered threshold. Because both modifier axes are active, it does not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified. Agreement with 7.61% within the 2 percentage-point resolution supports H-CORE; a substantially higher value would reject superlinear suppression without, by itself, establishing the linear-dilution model.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result from 3.80% to below 7.61% indicates partial suppression relative to linear dilution but does not meet the registered strong-suppression criterion. It would not cleanly select H-CORE or H-RESIN and would still leave H-RESIN versus H-DUAL unresolved.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, during a 120 C hold with viscosity recorded at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min across at least two independent preparations.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Identical deterministic VOI and hypothesis discrimination, but 17.5 wt% acrylic increases modifier burden without adding information.
Identical deterministic VOI and hypothesis discrimination, but 20 wt% acrylic is a larger chemistry perturbation than S1C41.
Identical deterministic VOI and hypothesis discrimination, but 22.5 wt% acrylic adds no mechanistic separation and further departs from the local chemistry.
Identical deterministic VOI and hypothesis discrimination, but 25 wt% acrylic has the greatest modifier burden among the tied cards.

It retains direct drift measurement and the same pairwise discrimination, but its 7.5 wt% minor-tackifier level lies outside the repeatedly supported 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster and carries a lower VOI of 0.687917.

proposer.reasoning: M-HOLD-120 directly measures the declared failure mode and the least-resolved coordinate, rather than inferring it through a thermal-shape model. S1C41 separates H-CORE from both low-drift hypotheses, remains within supported modifier regions, and minimizes modifier burden among the five exactly tied top cards. The experiment has moderate process-state risk, so its required independent repeats and recorded preparation histories are essential. It explicitly cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; that requires an acrylic-only hold comparison.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards have identical VOI components and separate the same two hypothesis pairs. S1C41 uses the smallest total modifier burden: 15 wt% AC1920 plus 5 wt% TK100. Both axes remain in supported regions, while this choice makes the smallest justified departure from the characterized reactive-core chemistry.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Changed from the tied-top dual-axis card S1C41::M-HOLD-120 to the lower-ranked acrylic-only card S1C49::M-HOLD-120. This evidence-based departure addresses a distinction the score's tied top set leaves unresolved: H-RESIN versus H-DUAL. M-HOLD-120 remains appropriate because it directly measures drift and does not transfer the unverified thermal-response shape. The preferred card should ultimately be embedded in the Skeptic's blocked contrast with unmodified E2 and S1C41.
residual_decision_risk: No measured unmodified-E2 120 C hold baseline is available, so an E1-derived linear-dilution comparator cannot uniquely attribute deviations to modifier suppression.
A single S1C49 run cannot complete the recommended blocked contrast with unmodified E2 and S1C41.

Large E2 realization-state variation and missing process-history fields could confound comparisons unless preparation order is randomized, process history is recorded, and independent preparations are used.
The rule for discordant repeats is not preregistered; thresholds should specify whether decisions use each repeat, the repeat mean, or an uncertainty bound.
AC1920 functionality is not verified; NCO:OH must be recalculated if it contains NCO-reactive groups.

The resin-modified chemistry lacks verified transferability of the shared 80-130 C thermal-response shape. M-HOLD-120 is directly applicable, but any later one-point reconstruction or shared-shape viscosity-level claim requires a direct M-SWEEP first.
Rheological suppression alone cannot establish the molecular explanation stated in H-RESIN.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The proposed direct hold remains a valid measurement of S1C41 drift, but its claimed H-CORE versus H-RESIN attribution relies on a 7.61% comparator imported from E1 even though S1C41 uses the different E2 reactive core. In addition, every member of the tied top set is dual-axis and leaves H-RESIN and H-DUAL entangled. Among explicitly identified cards, S1C49::M-HOLD-120 is the acrylic-only condition at the same 0.8000 reactive mass fraction as S1C41, so it supplies the missing modifier-axis contrast and can distinguish acrylic-only suppression from tackifier-required suppression. It still does not replace the required contemporaneous unmodified-E2 hold baseline; therefore its mechanistic interpretation must remain conditional until that baseline is measured.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The tied top set was unchanged in all 25 one-term perturbations: each weight was scaled from 0.5 to 1.5, top_experiment_set_stability was 1.0, and every recommendation_flip_boundary reports survival across the entire sweep. The base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower was 0.004583. Thus no tested perturbation makes S1C41::M-HOLD-120 cease to be top ranked. Weightings outside the tested range were not evaluated. This stability does not repair the scientific limitations of the E1-derived comparator or the unresolved H-RESIN versus H-DUAL contrast.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: S1C41 is outside the chemistry family supporting the shared temperature-response shape, but the proposed M-HOLD-120 primary endpoint does not use that shape and directly measures drift at 120 C. It is therefore chemistry-applicable for the drift endpoint. Any reconstruction of its 120-130 C response or viscosity-level coordinate from a one-point anchor would remain unsupported until a direct 80-130 C M-SWEEP verifies transferability for the AC1920+TK100 family.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The specified hold can directly return values below 3.80% or at or above 7.61%, so the numerical criteria are physically and procedurally attainable. The protocol should predefine whether decisions use every repeat, the mean, or an uncertainty bound. Attainability does not validate the E1-derived baseline for the E2-based candidate, so the resulting hypothesis attribution remains compromised until an E2 hold reference is measured.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The proposed result could not cleanly falsify H-CORE or support superlinear resin suppression, because the supposedly composition-specific linear-dilution baseline is imported from a different reactive core.
objections.objection: The claimed H-CORE versus H-RESIN separation uses 7.61% as the H-CORE prediction, calculated as the single-run E1 drift of 9.51% times S1C41's reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. S1C41, however, retains the E2 reactive core at NCO:OH 1.80, while E1 is a different core at NCO:OH 1.70. No E2 120 C hold drift has been measured. Therefore the experiment does not isolate departure from linear dilution of the actual E2 core; a result below or above 7.61% could reflect an E1-to-E2 core difference rather than modifier suppression.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low-drift result could only support the shared low-drift prediction; it could not establish whether acrylic alone is sufficient or whether the 5 wt% TK100 axis is required.
objections.objection: For S1C41 the registered predictions for H-RESIN and H-DUAL are identical at 3.804%, so their separation is 0 percentage points, below the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution. The proposer correctly lists "H-RESIN vs H-DUAL" under hypotheses_not_separated and states that an acrylic-only hold is required.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any observed suppression could be attributed only to the combined intervention. It could not be assigned to AC1920, TK100, their interaction, or simple dilution of the E2 core.
objections.objection: S1C41 simultaneously adds 15 wt% AC1920 and 5 wt% TK100 while reducing the E2 reactive core to 80 wt%. Thus acrylic addition, tackifier addition, and reactive-core dilution all move together. Without an acrylic-only condition at the same 0.8000 reactive mass fraction, modifier-axis attribution is unavailable; without a measured E2-core hold baseline, dilution attribution is also unavailable.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The observable itself remains interpretable, but discordant repeats could produce an undefined acceptance or falsification decision.
objections.objection: The primary observable survives this attack. SI_15_60 is calculated directly from viscosity measured at 15 and 60 minutes during the same 120 C hold; it requires no thermal-shape fit, temperature extrapolation, or imputation. However, the protocol does not specify whether the thresholds apply to each repeat, the repeat mean, or a confidence bound when repeats disagree.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No primary drift claim is lost. A problem would arise only if a one-point M-ANCHOR reconstruction or shared-shape-derived viscosity level were later used for S1C41 before a direct M-SWEEP verified transferability.
objections.objection: S1C41 is outside the measured unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI thermal-response family, but M-HOLD-120 does not reuse the shared 80-130 C response shape. The proposed primary observable is a direct isothermal measurement, so the proposal does not commit the prohibited shape transfer. This attack surface is therefore survived for the primary endpoint.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A mixed-repeat outcome may be adjudicated post hoc, and even a numerically decisive result may be given stronger mechanistic meaning than the design supports.
objections.objection: The apparatus can directly produce SI_15_60 values at or above 7.61% or below 3.80%, so the numerical criteria are attainable. Practical adjudication is nevertheless underspecified: "across at least two repeats" is defined for acceptance but the proposal does not state how H-RESIN falsification is handled if one repeat is at or above 7.61% and another is below it. More importantly, attaining either threshold does not repair the unmeasured E2 baseline.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A direct drift observation could be overstated as evidence for a molecular or chemical-inertness mechanism that the planned rheological protocol does not measure.
objections.objection: No target hold result or target-derived outcome label is visibly used. The proposal does, however, say that a low result "supports H-RESIN." Rheology alone can establish phenomenological suppression relative to a valid baseline, but it cannot establish H-RESIN's stated explanation that modifiers lower effective concentration and encounter frequency in a non-reactive continuum. In addition, the supplied stoichiometry note says true stoichiometry must be recalculated if either modifier has reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group; the hold measurement cannot establish modifier chemical inertness.

skeptic.recommended_change: Run a blocked, contemporaneous M-HOLD-120 contrast comprising the unmodified E2 reactive core, S1C49::M-HOLD-120 as the 20 wt% acrylic-only condition at reactive mass fraction 0.8000, and the proposed S1C41::M-HOLD-120 dual-axis condition at the same reactive mass fraction. Use the measured E2 drift, not E1 drift, to form the linear-dilution prediction for S1C41 and S1C49. Randomize preparation order, record the missing process-history fields, use independent preparations, and preregister whether threshold decisions are based on each repeat, the repeat mean, or a confidence bound. Verify modifier functionality or recalculate NCO:OH if AC1920 or TK100 contains NCO-reactive groups.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The 7.61% H-CORE comparator is derived from E1's single 9.51% hold run even though S1C41 uses the chemically and stoichiometrically different E2 core. Because E2 has no measured 120 C hold baseline, deviation from 7.61% cannot be uniquely attributed to resin suppression rather than an intrinsic E1-to-E2 core difference.

tool_trace.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This mandatory upstream audit must be loaded first to establish the chemistry provenance, state-shift evidence, hold contrast, and valid support of the local rheological regularities before any candidate or experiment comparison.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_R01_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 R01 day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is ADVISORY. Every experiment card above remains selectable, including the cards the audit marks inadmissible. Use the audit as scientific evidence and justify whatever you select.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.
